# round2.md — VisualCore: 25 Code-Generated Premium Games, Stage Two
**Authoritative second-stage implementation specification • November 10, 2026 • target location: repository root `/round2.md`**
**Document purpose:** implement 25 additional distinct premium casual 3D games **alongside** VisualCore and the original 25 applications. The first README one-shot plus all its D1/D2/D3 device tests **must already have finished with verifiable evidence** before this document may initiate any Stage Two feature. This is a *design and execution contract*, not a claim that code or device tests exist.
**Required artifact invariants:** OpenGL ES/EGL → owner ANGLE fork Metal backend; procedural meshes/GLSL/shader-based environments only; zero image-generation services, no manual texture/art/rigging dependency, no advertising, no ad SDK, no IAP, no subscriptions; paid once, complete offline game; independent gameplay identities; default simulator-first then one contiguous D1→D2→D3 physical-device campaign. Claude Code executes through the Claude Desktop app Code tab, **never** via a `claude` CLI subprocess.
**Design provenance:** final 25 and their scores are taken exactly from the owner-approved 500×62 scoring files; source AssertionOutlines are included verbatim in the appendix. Scores are subjective portfolio hypotheses, **not** measured market outcomes or predicted revenues. Hardware budgets are proposed test thresholds pending observation.

## Reader map and canonical precedence
1. Read and enforce `CLAUDE.md`, original `README.md`, and newly written `round2.md`; actual repository and toolchain evidence wins over assumed paths. If `README.md` implementation or device campaign is incomplete or unverifiable, do not start Stage Two. Continue original work instead.
2. This Stage Two design controls 25 new game requirements, while the original README remains authoritative for VisualCore baseline and first-25 contracts. Amend constitution with a nonconflicting explicit Round Two addendum; never silently erase established requirements.
3. The 34 new shared-framework feature specifications come first, and every feature has its complete Claude Desktop Spec Kit prompt sequence. Then come all 25 independent game specifications, each split into 10 complete scoped features with their own full Spec Kit commands and prompts.
4. Run preflight and feature audits, entire implementation + host/simulator testing, independent implementation-lock verification, sequential D1/D2/D3 device runs, fixes and final evidence. Do not treat CLI snippets as Claude agent automation; Python may orchestrate deterministic tools only.
5. The final appendix contains the original full 75 claims, 300 reasons and 300 evidence statements exactly as provided in the source research; the market study is also carried as an independently labelled source annex, without treating its projections as facts.

## 1. Mandatory Round One exit gate and owner-approved limits
**Do not bypass this gate merely because the root README is long.** Round One is only complete if the local repository contains verifiable implementation evidence for its VisualCore foundation, standalone Showcase, all original 25 product targets, full host/simulator campaign, and all **75 first-round app-device outcomes** on the recorded three physical devices. A completed Markdown checklist without the underlying artifacts fails this precondition.
### 1.1 Required gate assertions
1. **R1-EXIT-01:** Confirm current Git `HEAD`, branch and worktree status; never rewrite or clean user work without authorization. Inspect `git submodule status --recursive`, actual ProjectM/ANGLE pins, and license notices.
2. **R1-EXIT-02:** Check root `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` exist; test that the README extraction/runbook path is current. Preserve original first-25 source artifacts in place.
3. **R1-EXIT-03:** Locate real first-round code in `Packages/`, `Apps/`, `Configs/` and `scripts/` or equivalent current layout; do not blindly generate parallel duplicate packages. Record actual public APIs by compiling a small Showcase probe.
4. **R1-EXIT-04:** Collect command logs for all original 25 app build schemes and unit/simulator tests, matched to one source revision. Prohibit unsourced `PASS` rows.
5. **R1-EXIT-05:** Collect first-round implementation lock, simulator result bundle names, and Xcode configuration from `.autonomy/` or the repo equivalent, recording hashes and run IDs.
6. **R1-EXIT-06:** Collect 75 physical-device rows (D1×25, D2×25, D3×25), each with hardware ID, exact OS/build, app scheme/bundle, run timestamp, executable revision, artifact path, exit status, and evidence references.
7. **R1-EXIT-07:** For any first-round blocked physical test, determine whether the first-round gate truly permits proceeding; default to **NO**, preserving unresolved owner/system prerequisites rather than laundering a waiver.
8. **R1-EXIT-08:** Perform first-round performance reconciliation, app-target count, license scanner, ad/IAP SDK scanner and PrivacyInfo scan. Verify ordinary environment commands actually run on this Mac.
9. **R1-EXIT-09:** Compare compiled SDK declarations and EGL capabilities with the source reference. Build no Stage Two shaders until a real GL ES context can compile the minimal shader fixture.
10. **R1-EXIT-10:** Write signed-off machine-readable `docs/test-reports/round1-exit-audit.json` and Markdown summary, with tool outputs and SHA-256 manifest. Only an independent test command produces completion; the current Claude conversation is not evidence.
### 1.2 Device inventory carried forward, without guessed updates
| Role | Human readable device | Model | Recorded OS/build | Special obligation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | iPhone 15, device name `iPhone77` | `iPhone15,4` | iOS 27.0.1, `24A446` | Reference iPhone, small-screen layout, capture-specific original app tests only when applicable |
| D2 | iPad Pro 13-inch M5, `iPad77` | `iPad17,3` | iPadOS 27.2, `24B119` | Large-screen presentation, expected higher graphics headroom, not assumed until measured |
| D3 | iPad A16, `iPadC` | `iPad15,7` | iPadOS 26.5, `23F77` | Lowest-performance compatibility tier, **do not update this device** |
All three were recorded paired with Developer Mode enabled in the owner-supplied `devices.md` dated 2026-11-08; verify current live OS/build with `devicectl` each campaign. Do not publish results for other models and never confuse simulator identity with hardware. Signing credentials and device unlock are owner-controlled, and cannot be granted by an unattended document.
### 1.3 Hard product and implementation guardrails
- Every game must run entirely offline in the absence of accounts, downloads and server services; no network telemetry or ad network dependencies. Internet can be used by the development machine to fetch toolchains and pinned source only.
- The complete price is a single App Store purchase. No StoreKit product queries, in-app purchases, virtual currency, subscriptions, paywalls after install, ads, cross-promotion ads, affiliate tracking, advertising identifiers or SDKs.
- Gameplay code must never require external raster-image generation or manual sculpting/rigging. Code may generate meshes, masks, gradients, vector UI, icons, shader textures and screenshots; generated outputs and their generator sources must be reproducible.
- Touch input is the primary control scheme; game completion must not require a keyboard, mouse, game controller, network, motion sensors, microphone, camera or device location.
- Swift/SwiftPM owns game models, score/persistence and native UI; C++/Objective-C++ bridges only when justified by concrete existing EGL interfaces; GLSL ES runs through the existing ANGLE Metal path.
- No use of private iOS APIs, dynamic loading workarounds, hidden entitlements, prohibited capture APIs, or monkey-patching framework binaries. Log legal and licensing checks.
- Target the recorded OS set and inspect actual iOS deployment values in project.yml; never raise minimum OS to eliminate D3 failures.
- Every requirement has a traceable test and evidence artifact; tasks are checked only after independent rerun, not through model self-report.
- Commit with ordinary descriptive messages (no fabricated co-authorship trailers); no unauthorized remote push, App Store Connect action, certificates, signing changes or device OS changes. Owner grants from the ProjectM repository do not automatically cover VisualCore.
- Use at most 10 agents overall, one writer per file and one physical-device/test lane per Mac. Compile failures block dependent gates; temporary build artifacts stay gitignored.

### 2.1 Public contracts to stabilize before game work
```swift
public struct GameSeed: Codable, Hashable { public let value: UInt64 }
public struct SimulationTick: Comparable, Codable { public let rawValue: UInt64 }
public struct GameInput: Codable {
  public var tick: SimulationTick
  public var controlID: String
  public var normalizedX: Double
  public var normalizedY: Double
  public var amount: Double
}
public struct GameResult: Codable {
  public enum Status: String, Codable { case ongoing, won, failed, blocked }
  public var status: Status
  public var score: Int
  public var diagnosticCodes: [String]
}
public protocol DeterministicPuzzleState: Codable {
  associatedtype Action: Codable
  mutating func apply(_ action: Action) throws
  mutating func step(fixedDeltaSeconds: Double) throws
  func result() -> GameResult
  func canonicalDigest() throws -> String
}
public struct GameSceneDescriptor: Codable {
  public var seed: GameSeed
  public var contentVersion: Int
  public var visualQuality: Int
  public var cameraPose: [Double] // serialized, validated projection parameters
  public var colorAccessibilityMode: String
  public var reducedMotion: Bool
}
// Interfaces are semantic examples. Inspect actual Stage One VisualCore types
// before implementing; prefer adapters to breaking public API or duplicate contexts.
```
All game engines are CPU-testable without initializing ANGLE. Gameplay advances in integer ticks and emits immutable render snapshots. Rendering is a consumer of snapshots, never the hidden owner of success/failure. Resource creation and destruction occur on the correct GL context thread; SwiftUI owns high-level navigation and accessibility. Graphics tests compare **semantic state** exactly and image appearance with documented platform-appropriate tolerances, not byte-for-byte pixels across different GPUs.
### 2.2 Quality and performance acceptance (proposals until D1–D3 measurement)
| Metric | Initial internal target | Evidence and nonnegotiable rule |
|---|---|---|
| Display cadence | Seek 60 fps, allow adaptive quality tier | Device `CADisplayLink` on-time frame ledger + physical capture; record actual refresh and display configuration. Target is not a claim about results. |
| Response latency | Target median input-to-visible change under 80 ms, p95 under 150 ms | record monotonic event and displayed result times on same clock; collect real device observations |
| Stable logic | identical per-seed checksums at fixed tick sequence | SwiftPM/Linux/host replay fixtures; no GPU readback used to declare win |
| Sustained run | 30-minute D3 on every app, with no unreported thermal failure | per-interval frame, memory, CPU, GPU where genuinely available, thermal state and crash summaries |
| Levels | planned ~70–100 per app, as specified later | a content generator plus solver witness for every shipped level, no dummy levels |
| Launch | first meaningful interaction should avoid blocking shader compile | prewarm bounded program variants; track cold/warm startup separately |
| Flash reduction | avoid rapid high-contrast full-screen transitions | test Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing and user opt-in brightness settings; never eliminate visual information needed to win |
| Privacy | offline local save and no ad tracking | signed binary/static dependency inspection + on-device container diff |
| Content fidelity | full gameplay rather than looping demo | XCUITest reaches win, failure, undo, replay, replay persistence for every game |
| Distinctiveness | all apps must have unique player input/goal/progression + visual signature | human review before store release; no auto-permission to publish clones |

## 3. Spec Kit and Claude Desktop integration: invocation rules
The active Claude Desktop Code session must inspect `.claude/skills/` after the initial Round One setup and **invoke each `/speckit-*` skill as a separate conversational action**. The textual sequences below are complete prompts for those skills, not shell lines for Terminal. A single text message listing ten slash commands may not invoke them: execute one skill, inspect its file outputs, then invoke the next. If the installed skill naming differs, use the actual installed skill names and record the mapping. Do not use `claude -p`, `claude` subprocesses, or unsanctioned agent SDK loops.
```bash
# Terminal commands are for deterministic Spec Kit setup and verification ONLY.
# Do not rerun `specify init` over a working Stage One repository without inspection.
specify --help
specify integration --help
find .claude/skills -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md -print
# Existing project missing Claude integration: inspect --help then provision with a supported command:
specify integration install claude
# If initialization truly absent in a NEW empty repo, only after backed-up audit:
# specify init . --integration claude --script py --non-interactive
# Never execute the following in a shell: /speckit-specify ...
```
Spec Kit stores the active feature in `.specify/feature.json` (or overrides via `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`), not necessarily the current Git branch; the Desktop agent must verify the active target before *each* skill. When switching to feature N, update the active feature state using installed Spec Kit workflows, and assert the generated spec path matches N. Independently allocate globally unique `R2-*` requirements/tests/task IDs; do not reuse the first-round identifiers. Use an audit ledger with states `NOT_STARTED`, `SPECIFIED`, `PLANNED`, `TASKED`, `IMPLEMENTING`, `VERIFIED_HOST`, `VERIFIED_SIM`, `CONVERGED`, `BLOCKED`, `VERIFIED_DEVICE` and `RELEASE_REVIEW_PENDING`.
**Explicit close-loop:** `/speckit-converge` must be called for **every** new shared feature and every game subfeature. It is not optional. If convergence appends tasks, loop `/speckit-implement` → real test commands → `/speckit-converge` until truly converged. A single command invocation or a model-written `[X]` is not sufficient evidence. Only then advance the dependency graph. At the end, run an additional suite-level `/speckit-converge` across cross-feature contracts.

### 3.1 Constitution amendment — complete `/speckit-constitution` prompt (invoke once)
```text
/speckit-constitution Update the EXISTING VisualCore constitutional rules with a non-destructive Stage Two amendment. Treat original README Stage One and its first 25 app device evidence as a hard prerequisite; add 25 additional code-only premium games in the same repository. Preserve the audited OpenGL ES/EGL → owner ANGLE Metal backend and ProjectM source/fork/license boundaries. Require real procedural GLSL/mesh/particle graphics, complete original gameplay and seeded solver-certified content; no raster image generation, hand-made 3D assets, advertisements, ad SDKs, paid IAP, subscriptions, network requirements, unlicensed third-party art or copied game identity. Every proposed Stage Two shared feature and game subfeature MUST execute specify → clarify → plan → checklist → tasks → analyze → implement → converge with independent evidence; preserve prior constitution requirements and write a dated compatibility ADR for any conflict. Implement all apps and simulator checks before physical-device runs. Only after verified Round Two lock run all 25 apps on D1 then D2 then D3; never update D3 iPadOS 26.5. Protect signing, credentials, personal/private data, Apple store actions and device trust. The Claude Desktop Code session is the sole coding agent; no Claude CLI subprocess or agent SDK supervisor. Verify every checkbox by executed tests and do not infer positive market outcomes from concept scores. Preserve the full 2026-11-10 owner ProjectM playbook through the existing root CLAUDE.md, do not delete it.
```
The constitution is a project-wide operation, not something to rerun destructively for each feature. Run it once immediately after Round One exit inspection, inspect the resulting diff and resolve blocking conflicts in an ADR. If an installed Spec Kit skill does not support updating an existing constitution, follow the versioned feature-preserving update path from its actual documentation.
### 3.2 Large-document, bounded-context retrieval for Claude Desktop
This `round2.md` is intentionally multi-megabyte. Do NOT try to ingest every line into a single Claude context: retrieve canonical rules, the dependency table and ONLY the currently active feature subsection using local text search and bounded reads, then write a short evidence-grounded session summary. During a game feature consult the full game design and relevant original AssertionOutline, not all other 24 games. Preserve the complete document on disk and validate its hash before using it. `rg`/`sed` are deterministic terminal tools; they do not invoke Claude CLI.
```bash
# Examples for the Desktop Code agent's terminal tool, not for model invocation:
rg -n '^## [0-9]+\.|^#### R2-F|^### [0-9][0-9]\.|^##### R2-G' round2.md > Build/round2/document-index.txt
rg -n '^#### R2-F08:|^#### R2-F09:' round2.md
rg -n '^### 01\. Aurora Loom|^### 02\. Lissajous Labyrinth' round2.md
# Read bounded line ranges around the active section using discovered line numbers.
# For a full argument, locate the corresponding source inside section 11.1.
# Never summarize missing portions as if they were read.
```
Suggested session memory file: `.autonomy/round2-active-context.md` contains active feature ID, line range, accepted decisions, code paths, exact verification commands, actual evidence files, current source SHA and next step, and is regenerated after every successful gate. This is a retrieval aid, not an alternative source of truth. The enormous historical 500-game research annex is for provenance, not mandatory reading on each implementation step.

#### R2-F01: Round 1 evidence & reproducible baseline audit
**Required games:** ALL. **Prior features:** round-one exit verification. **Deliverable:** verify repo status; prior 25 app builds; simulator results; D1-D3 campaign; tool versions; git pins. **Spec directory:** `specs/201-round-1-evidence-reproducible-baseline-audit/`. **Main responsibility:** implement only missing Stage Two capability behind tested public contracts; no Stage One breakage.
**Complete acceptance definition:** create exact CPU reference and deterministic seed fixtures where applicable; include shader compile and context-lifecycle test if GPU-facing; document failure and memory ownership; support iOS 26.5 APIs or guard later ones; implement a semantic test independent of screenshot-based beauty; add simulator UI test if public-facing; create traceable log and SHA-256 run evidence. Do not mark as passed until a fresh command run returns success.
**Proposed engineering work items:**
- **API audit:** Inventory the Stage One symbols and existing packages related to Round 1 evidence & reproducible baseline audit; record signatures and ABI/availability constraints before selecting an adapter.
- **Pure model:** Implement parameter validation, versioned serialization and deterministic reference behavior for verify repo status; prior 25 app builds; simulator results; D1-D3 campaign; tool versions; git pins.
- **Integration:** Wire Round 1 evidence & reproducible baseline audit into the existing rendering boundary without creating another EGL context or imposing ProjectM engine dependencies.
- **Shader and resource safety:** Compile all GLSL ES variants against the real ANGLE-backed context; use explicit buffer ownership, safe retirement and context-loss rehydration.
- **Golden tests:** Write at least five positive, negative and boundary fixtures for Round 1 evidence & reproducible baseline audit, including bad input, missing capability and seed replay.
- **Documents:** Update `docs/architecture/` and feature ADRs; record applicability to ALL, with rejected alternatives and source links.
- **Observability:** Emit stable feature ID R2-F01, current app ID, seed, tick, capability tier and reason code for every failure report.
- **Finish gate:** Independent host/simulator check, specification coverage matrix, copyright/asset scan, `/speckit-converge` reports Converged.

### 4.3 Round Two expanded engineering contracts — binding supplement to all 34 feature prompts

These decisions extend rather than replace the original `R2-F01`–`R2-F34` specifications above. Every feature must be audited for genuine reuse before implementation. A claimed API that has not been found, compiled and tested in the local checkout is only a **proposal**. Preserve the ProjectM / ANGLE owner-fork pins; do not fork a second graphics backend.

| Workstream | Proposed file families | Producers and consumers | Independent gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU puzzle models | `Packages/GameRuleKernel/Sources`, `Packages/GameRuleKernel/Tests` | All 25 games; immutable `GameSnapshot`, tagged `GameAction`, explicit `RuleResult` | Two CPUs / simulator action traces replay to identical canonical hashes |
| Deterministic solvers | `Packages/GameSolvers`, `Packages/LevelCertification` | All games; family-specific shortest path, grid search, analytic residual, physics bounds | 100 proposed levels per game must eventually have real solver witnesses; count zero placeholders |
| OpenGL ES renderer | `Packages/VisualCore`, `Packages/ANGLERendering`, `Packages/ProceduralEffects` | Rendering adapters only; existing ANGLE → Metal path remains authoritative | Real shader compilation and `glGetError` checks, GLES/extension fingerprints recorded on D1–D3 |
| Procedural asset compilation | `Packages/ProceduralMeshes`, `Packages/ProceduralTextures` | Analytic surfaces, flora, tubes, faceted mesh, heightfield and SDF; no image model or manual art | Repeat build with same code/seed yields identical logical artifact hashes |
| Gameplay accessibility | `Packages/GameUXKit`, `Packages/GameInput` | Every app, including alternatives to drag, tap precision, color, motion and audio | Semantic XCUITest and accessible gameplay replay |
| Content provenance | `docs/games/<slug>/levels`, `scripts/generate_levels.py`, `scripts/validate_levels.py` | Seed registry, complete solver action witnesses, level schemas, uniqueness decisions | Parse and validate **all** shipped level manifests; verify no claimed level exists only in this Markdown file |
| Evidence engine | `scripts/run_simulator_campaign.py`, `scripts/run_device_campaign.py`, `docs/test-reports/round2` | XcodeGen schemes, devicectl, XCTest, `.xcresult` and in-app JSON; tests gated after implementation lock | Actual signed device ID, OS/build and build SHA, with no simulator/device result conflation |
| Market/legal hygiene | `scripts/check_compliance.py`, `docs/legal/game-distinctiveness.md` | Every game and release candidate | No advertising, IAP, subscriptions, private APIs or misleading clone branding in built app or linked frameworks |

**Public API design sketches (not assertions that existing code exports these exact names).** Make wrapper protocols only when the live repository lacks an equivalent. Prefer thin compatibility adapters rather than rewriting the stable engine.

```swift
public struct GameTick: Hashable, Codable, Sendable { public let value: UInt64 }
public struct GameActionEnvelope<Action: Codable & Sendable>: Codable, Sendable {
    public let tick: GameTick
    public let sequence: UInt32
    public let action: Action
}
public struct LevelIdentity: Hashable, Codable, Sendable {
    public let gameID: String
    public let levelID: String
    public let seed: UInt64
    public let schemaVersion: UInt32
}
public enum RuleRejection: Error, Codable, Sendable {
    case invalidControl, outOfBounds, blockedGeometry, insufficientBudget, staleSequence
}
public protocol DeterministicGameModel: Sendable {
    associatedtype Action: Codable & Sendable
    associatedtype Snapshot: Codable & Sendable
    mutating func apply(_ command: GameActionEnvelope<Action>) throws(RuleRejection)
    mutating func advanceFixedTick()
    func snapshot() -> Snapshot
}
```

The pseudocode above needs Swift compiler/version verification before adoption; typed throws and generic Codable synthesis must be checked against the actual pinned Swift toolchain. Do **not** treat the sketch as compiled source. If typed throws is unavailable, use ordinary `throws` plus a typed validation layer. No gameplay input or graphics result depends on the user's network connection.

**Optical-effect truth boundary:** bloom, reflective-looking colors, translucency approximations, and caustic-looking gradients are presentation approximations; no claim of physically exact simulation is required. The CPU domain still computes ray intersections, phases, conservation or projection as appropriate. D3 quality may trade samples, layers and resolution while keeping scene semantics identical.

**Compiler and artifact rule:** never use a passed simulator command as proof of D1, D2 or D3 frame pacing. Record `.xcresult` bundles, command exit status, the app binary SHA-256, and an in-app result export with per-sample IDs. `BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION`, `NOT_RUN`, and `PASS` are distinct states. A device run must not start until a verified Round Two implementation-lock manifest is present and complete.

**Spec Kit amendment order:** execute all existing feature prompts in section 4.2; then test these common contracts using a bounded cross-feature task batch. Any new build or API deficiency becomes a new uniquely numbered task with full `/speckit-*` progression, not a clandestine shortcut. Review the actual `.claude/skills` directory before assuming `/speckit-converge` is installed.

## 6. Game-by-game implementation blueprints — 25 independently complete products
**Interpretation rules:** Each blueprint establishes a *proposed implementable decision*; any quantitative constants are initial acceptance-contract values, adjustable only by recorded ADR and test proof. None of the named algorithms is claimed already implemented. Games must each have at least one actual 3D interaction, win/fail state, solved/proven level catalog, pause/replay and offline progress. “Fifty generated levels” here means a deterministic, solver-certified production catalog, not copied/random cosmetic scenes.
### 01. Aurora Loom — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G01` • **Source candidate:** `G162` • **Category:** Light and color • **Comparative rank:** 1/25 • **Research score:** 94.8/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $2.99 upfront • **Content target:** 80 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies. **Signature spectacle:** camera-depth layered auroral silk with refractive-looking interference. **Objective:** make three luminous ribbons share a target harmonic phase at four gates. **A failure:** phase mismatch exceeds gate tolerance after the move allowance. **A victory:** all four gate samples stay within angular tolerance for two complete periods.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific spectral ribbon phase system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag an anchor to displace a ribbon, rotate an orbital dial to change phase; two-finger pan camera. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.1.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** spectral ribbon phase. **Proposed authoritative law:** A ribbon is a swept cubic spline with phase q(s,t)=k*s+omega*t+phi; controls quantize k and phi into sixteen stable ticks. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is bounded phase-gradient coordinate descent with exact grid search fallback. **Truth metric:** wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all four gate samples stay within angular tolerance for two complete periods” using `wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “phase mismatch exceeds gate tolerance after the move allowance”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.

#### 6.1.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** camera-depth layered auroral silk with refractive-looking interference. **Required geometry:** parallel transport ribbon frame with bevel edge shading. **Signature shader:** Layered ribbon meshes with wave displacement and fragment interference patterns. **Palette:** polar teal, magenta, acid-gold. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.1.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 80 levels. **Prototype:** 12 handcrafted-feeling deterministic phase puzzles then seeded variations. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.
**Per-level planned content manifest.** Every line below is a *requirement for generating and certifying an individual stage*, not a statement that the level currently exists. Values are stable derived design seeds/metadata; actual target parameters and solver witness must be generated and stored at build time.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.1.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/AuroraLoom/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.1.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `ribbon` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Phase mismatch exceeds gate tolerance after the move allowance”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.

#### 6.1.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** overdraw and visual similarity to Backwards Aurora. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `ribbon` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `AuroraLoom` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `camera-depth layered auroral silk with refractive-looking interference`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `AuroraLoom` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `camera-depth layered auroral silk with refractive-looking interference`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `AuroraLoom` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `camera-depth layered auroral silk with refractive-looking interference`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.1.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** overdraw and visual similarity to Backwards Aurora. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `weave` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.1.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Aurora Loom
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** make three luminous ribbons share a target harmonic phase at four gates. **CPU domain:** spectral ribbon phase. **Ground-truth metric:** wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check. **Candidate solver:** bounded phase-gradient coordinate descent with exact grid search fallback. The visual identity is camera-depth layered auroral silk with refractive-looking interference. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.1.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/aurora-loom/App/AuroraLoomApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/aurora-loom/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/aurora-loom/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/aurora-loom/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/aurora-loom/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/aurora-loom/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Domain/AuroraLoomState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Domain/AuroraLoomAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Domain/AuroraLoomRules.swift` | Implement wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Domain/AuroraLoomSolver.swift` | Implement bounded phase-gradient coordinate descent with exact grid search fallback | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate parallel-transport ribbon mesh and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/aurora-loom/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/aurora-loomUITests/AuroraLoomUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/aurora-loom/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/aurora-loom/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/aurora-loom/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

#### 6.1.17. Architectural decision ledger — explicit choices and failure semantics
| ID | Decision to implement | Why this is required for this particular game | Verification before acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-G01-ADR-01` | **Canonical state and serialization.** Define a stable versioned schema. Separate player controls, discrete puzzle objects, authored level parameters, solver witness and visual-only particle state. | In **Aurora Loom**, `four gate phase congruence` is the rule-level requirement while `parallel-transport ribbon mesh` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against angle wrap around ±π; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G01-ADR-02` | **Fixed-step scheduling.** Use integer tick count and a bounded accumulator; cap accumulated elapsed time after suspension; never use display refresh delta as a victory predicate. | In **Aurora Loom**, `spline tangent continuity` is the rule-level requirement while `phase-colored emissive fringe` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against zero-tangent spline segment; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G01-ADR-03` | **Control discretization.** Quantize the five listed gestures into distinct command cases with stable IDs; deterministic rounding rules must be identical in simulator and device builds. | In **Aurora Loom**, `wrapped residual at samples` is the rule-level requirement while `layered optical-depth strips` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against ribbon crossing visually hides a gate; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.1.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Aurora Loom law: `A ribbon is a swept cubic spline with phase q(s,t)=k*s+omega*t+phi; controls quantize k and phi into sixteen stable ticks`. The source of truth is `wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.1.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Aurora Loom must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are phase-shift, route, twist, anchor, weave. Its unique win predicate is wrapped phase residual, no aesthetic-only success check. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 02. Lissajous Labyrinth — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G02` • **Source candidate:** `G456` • **Category:** Wave mathematics • **Comparative rank:** 2/25 • **Research score:** 94.3/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $2.99 upfront • **Content target:** 90 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.004167 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Tune two coupled frequencies so a moving point traces a safe path. **Signature spectacle:** luminous ink threads composing a slow-motion 3D mathematical flower. **Objective:** tune two integer frequency ratios and phases so a tracer passes every illuminated checkpoint without contacting hazards. **A failure:** the point enters an obstacle volume during its required lap. **A victory:** all checkpoints visited in order over a complete fundamental period.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific three-axis harmonic path planning system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.
#### 6.2.1. Player journey and minute-by-minute first play
- **T+0 seconds (design goal):** Splash and immediate readable hero demo. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.0.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
- **T+10 seconds (design goal):** One accessible instruction and first safe action. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.10.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
- **T+30 seconds (design goal):** First actual choice that can succeed or fail. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.30.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
- **T+60 seconds (design goal):** Solve or intentionally reset a first challenge. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.60.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
- **T+120 seconds (design goal):** Move from tutorial to varied second puzzle. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.120.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
- **T+180 seconds (design goal):** Understand progression, undo and pause. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.180.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
- **T+300 seconds (design goal):** Reach a surprising spectacle event and demonstrate replay. Show frequency manipulation explicitly; controls: rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.lissajous-labyrinth.300.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.
**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** rotate the dual dials for frequency and phase; tap preview and trace scrubber. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.2.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** three-axis harmonic path planning. **Proposed authoritative law:** x=A*sin(a*t+phi), y=B*sin(b*t), z=C*cos(c*t+psi); ratios from 1:1 to 9:8 with rational periods. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.004167 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is enumerate coprime frequency pairs and phase offsets with segment-swept collision tests. **Truth metric:** minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all checkpoints visited in order over a complete fundamental period” using `minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “the point enters an obstacle volume during its required lap”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G02` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct LissajousLabyrinthLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct LissajousLabyrinthState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: tune two integer frequency ratios and phases so a tracer passes every illuminated checkpoint without contacting hazards.
// Model: x=A*sin(a*t+phi), y=B*sin(b*t), z=C*cos(c*t+psi); ratios from 1:1 to 9:8 with rational periods.
// Solver: enumerate coprime frequency pairs and phase offsets with segment-swept collision tests.
```

#### 6.2.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** luminous ink threads composing a slow-motion 3D mathematical flower. **Required geometry:** adaptive curve tessellation with tangent-space width. **Signature shader:** elegant 3D luminous harmonic curves weave through obstacles; Analytic oscillators, Fourier curve meshes, interference heightfields and emissive color. **Palette:** cobalt, violet and copper. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.2.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 90 levels. **Prototype:** guided 3-stage tutorial followed by frequency puzzles with generated obstacles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

#### 6.2.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/LissajousLabyrinth/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.2.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `frequency` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “The point enters an obstacle volume during its required lap”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.2.11. Exact simulator-first executable acceptance matrix
The matrix below is **not a statement of passed tests**. It is the complete planned test registry. Every row must map to an actual automated test function or harness automation mode. A non-applicable test must carry a documented reason, not a silent omission. Platform variants are separate: unit/host is logic proof; iOS 26.5 simulator is compatibility/UI proof; iOS 27.2 simulator is newer SDK behavior proof; actual D1–D3 graphics results come only after Round Two lock.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-G02-T001-host-logic` | host-logic | First launch | Seed=f89a52f5f0; initialize frequency at a known valid fixture, apply a deterministic action sequence. | minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order computed from CPU reference; stable digest and clear error code; save `result.json` plus command log. |
| `R2-G02-T001-sim-ios26` | sim-ios26 | First launch | Seed=6e90a9b73f; initialize frequency at a known valid fixture, apply a deterministic action sequence. | Sim iOS 26.5 loads adaptive curve tessellation with tangent-space width without availability crash; XCTest verifies a single interaction and native text communicate the win condition immediately; archive `.xcresult` and screenshot. |

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
#### 6.2.12. Seed-by-seed production-level acceptance and replay contracts
Each numbered stage has *seven mandatory acceptance facets* produced by deterministic test generation. Output below enumerates the complete release catalog: QA should create all indicated artifacts and compare them to `ContentManifest.json`. The same replay witness is consumed by CPU-only unit tests and by simulator gameplay on a selected stratified subset. A stage that lacks one facet is `BLOCKED_CONTENT`, not `PASSED`.

#### 6.2.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** aliasing and difficult-to-read overlapping curves. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `frequency` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `LissajousLabyrinth` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `luminous ink threads composing a slow-motion 3D mathematical flower`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `LissajousLabyrinth` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `luminous ink threads composing a slow-motion 3D mathematical flower`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `LissajousLabyrinth` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `luminous ink threads composing a slow-motion 3D mathematical flower`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.2.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** aliasing and difficult-to-read overlapping curves. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `tune` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.2.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Lissajous Labyrinth
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** tune two integer frequency ratios and phases so a tracer passes every illuminated checkpoint without contacting hazards. **CPU domain:** three-axis harmonic path planning. **Ground-truth metric:** minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order. **Candidate solver:** enumerate coprime frequency pairs and phase offsets with segment-swept collision tests. The visual identity is luminous ink threads composing a slow-motion 3D mathematical flower. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

| `docs/games/lissajous-labyrinth/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/lissajous-labyrinth/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/lissajous-labyrinth/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.2.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Lissajous Labyrinth law: `x=A*sin(a*t+phi), y=B*sin(b*t), z=C*cos(c*t+psi); ratios from 1:1 to 9:8 with rational periods`. The source of truth is `minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.2.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Lissajous Labyrinth must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are tune frequency, offset phase, set amplitude, rotate viewpoint, commit trajectory. Its unique win predicate is minimum segment-obstacle clearance and checkpoint arc order. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 03. Wave Knot Keeper — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G03` • **Source candidate:** `G466` • **Category:** Wave mathematics • **Comparative rank:** 3/25 • **Research score:** 94.3/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $2.99 upfront • **Content target:** 72 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Drag spectral control points to untie closed three-dimensional wave knots. **Signature spectacle:** glasslike light ropes braided through space with beat-driven caustic pulses. **Objective:** move spectral handles until one closed knot matches a designated untangled embedding while preserving strand continuity. **A failure:** a restricted segment intersection or tension bound violation occurs. **A victory:** projected signed crossing graph and knot invariant satisfy the target configuration.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific topological strand manipulation system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.
