#### 6.6.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** time loops can feel opaque without ghost previews. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `timeline` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `ChronoConstellator` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `glowing temporal ribbons resembling a woven astronomical score`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `ChronoConstellator` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `glowing temporal ribbons resembling a woven astronomical score`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `ChronoConstellator` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `glowing temporal ribbons resembling a woven astronomical score`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.6.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** time loops can feel opaque without ghost previews. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `record` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.6.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Chrono Constellator
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** record short time loops of orbiting stars so their luminous trails coincide with a target constellation. **CPU domain:** time-based synchronized star routing. **Ground-truth metric:** tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy. **Candidate solver:** integer-tick phase search for replay windows and time offsets. The visual identity is glowing temporal ribbons resembling a woven astronomical score. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.6.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/chrono-constellator/App/ChronoConstellatorApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/chrono-constellator/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/chrono-constellator/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/chrono-constellator/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/chrono-constellator/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/chrono-constellator/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Domain/ChronoConstellatorState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Domain/ChronoConstellatorAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Domain/ChronoConstellatorRules.swift` | Implement tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Domain/ChronoConstellatorSolver.swift` | Implement integer-tick phase search for replay windows and time offsets | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate temporal ribbon trails and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/chrono-constellator/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/chrono-constellatorUITests/ChronoConstellatorUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/chrono-constellator/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/chrono-constellator/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/chrono-constellator/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

#### 6.6.17. Architectural decision ledger — explicit choices and failure semantics
| ID | Decision to implement | Why this is required for this particular game | Verification before acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-G06-ADR-01` | **Canonical state and serialization.** Define a stable versioned schema. Separate player controls, discrete puzzle objects, authored level parameters, solver witness and visual-only particle state. | In **Chrono Constellator**, `event log tick integrity` is the rule-level requirement while `temporal ribbon trails` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against non-deterministic replay; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G06-ADR-02` | **Fixed-step scheduling.** Use integer tick count and a bounded accumulator; cap accumulated elapsed time after suspension; never use display refresh delta as a victory predicate. | In **Chrono Constellator**, `snapshot hash equality` is the rule-level requirement while `ghost orbits and timestamps` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against history exhaustion; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G06-ADR-03` | **Control discretization.** Quantize the five listed gestures into distinct command cases with stable IDs; deterministic rounding rules must be identical in simulator and device builds. | In **Chrono Constellator**, `synchronized occupancy` is the rule-level requirement while `star flare billboards generated in shader` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against unspecified rewind semantics; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G06-ADR-04` | **World and camera coordinates.** Adopt right-handed world units, explicit view/projection matrices, stable near/far planes and reversible touch-to-world mapping for every selectable handle. | In **Chrono Constellator**, `collision-free replay` is the rule-level requirement while `time cursor ring` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against frame-rate changes game state; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G06-ADR-05` | **Puzzle invariants.** Centralize source-of-truth checks on the CPU; each accepted action either produces a new consistent state or returns an explicit typed rejection. | In **Chrono Constellator**, `bounded loop period` is the rule-level requirement while `interference pulses on lock` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.6.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Chrono Constellator must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are record window, shift timeline, phase orbit, rewind, play synchronized loop. Its unique win predicate is tick-accurate replay hash and synchronized target-cell occupancy. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 07. Amethyst Escape — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G07` • **Source candidate:** `G299` • **Category:** Crystal solids • **Comparative rank:** 7/25 • **Research score:** 93.99/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 80 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Rotate crystalline layers to open a route for a rolling pearl. **Signature spectacle:** layered amethyst gem cathedral with dancing internal facet highlights. **Objective:** rotate nested crystal shells to align apertures and roll a pearl from center to exit. **A failure:** pearl enters a blocked wedge or move budget expires. **A victory:** pearl moves through the designated exit gap in the outer shell.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific nested faceted 3D maze system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.
#### 6.7.1. Player journey and minute-by-minute first play

No ad gate, account, tutorial wall or “rate us” nag. Capture a `firstPlay.amethyst-escape.0.json` UI milestone during an automated simulator journey. Timing is a design target until real usability tests exist.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag each shell bezel, tap advance pearl, double tap isolate layer. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.7.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** nested faceted 3D maze. **Proposed authoritative law:** shell rings rotate in fixed increments; connectivity graph is recomputed at angle changes; pearl uses deterministic pocket transitions. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is breadth-first search over discretized shell angles and pearl pocket indices. **Truth metric:** graph route length and reachable exit proof.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “pearl moves through the designated exit gap in the outer shell” using `graph route length and reachable exit proof`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “pearl enters a blocked wedge or move budget expires”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G07` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct AmethystEscapeLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct AmethystEscapeState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: rotate nested crystal shells to align apertures and roll a pearl from center to exit.
// Model: shell rings rotate in fixed increments; connectivity graph is recomputed at angle changes; pearl uses deterministic pocket transitions.
// Solver: breadth-first search over discretized shell angles and pearl pocket indices.
```

#### 6.7.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** layered amethyst gem cathedral with dancing internal facet highlights. **Required geometry:** procedurally beveled wedge polyhedra with analytic faceting. **Signature shader:** translucent nested polygons with shifting specular highlights; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Palette:** amethyst purple and cool platinum. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.7.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 80 levels. **Prototype:** 12 instructional radial mazes and 68 generated nested-shell boards. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.7.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/AmethystEscape/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.7.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `shell` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `graph route length and reachable exit proof`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Pearl enters a blocked wedge or move budget expires”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.
#### 6.7.8. Complete app file inventory and module boundaries
| Expected repository file | Ownership and reason |
|---|---|
| `Apps/AmethystEscape/App/AmethystEscapeApp.swift` | @main scene and application lifecycle, no direct shader logic |
| `Apps/AmethystEscape/App/AmethystEscapeCoordinator.swift` | session navigation and restoration, entitlement-free paid-once app |
| `Apps/AmethystEscape/App/RootScene.swift` | SwiftUI view hierarchy with exactly one GL rendering host |
| `Apps/AmethystEscape/UI/AmethystEscapeHUD.swift` | accessible goal and state readout |
| `Apps/AmethystEscape/UI/AmethystEscapeGestureOverlay.swift` | arbitrate touch, choose depth-aware world target |
| `Apps/AmethystEscape/UI/AmethystEscapeLevelPicker.swift` | campaign catalog, progress and seed previews |

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.

#### 6.7.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** translucency sorting and occluded controls. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `shell` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** graph route length and reachable exit proof stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `AmethystEscape` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `layered amethyst gem cathedral with dancing internal facet highlights`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `AmethystEscape` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `layered amethyst gem cathedral with dancing internal facet highlights`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `AmethystEscape` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `layered amethyst gem cathedral with dancing internal facet highlights`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.7.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** translucency sorting and occluded controls. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `rotate` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.7.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Amethyst Escape
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** rotate nested crystal shells to align apertures and roll a pearl from center to exit. **CPU domain:** nested faceted 3D maze. **Ground-truth metric:** graph route length and reachable exit proof. **Candidate solver:** breadth-first search over discretized shell angles and pearl pocket indices. The visual identity is layered amethyst gem cathedral with dancing internal facet highlights. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.7.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/amethyst-escape/App/AmethystEscapeApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/amethyst-escape/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/amethyst-escape/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/amethyst-escape/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/amethyst-escape/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/amethyst-escape/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Domain/AmethystEscapeState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Domain/AmethystEscapeAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Domain/AmethystEscapeRules.swift` | Implement graph route length and reachable exit proof | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Domain/AmethystEscapeSolver.swift` | Implement breadth-first search over discretized shell angles and pearl pocket indices | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate faceted polyhedral shells and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/amethyst-escape/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/amethyst-escapeUITests/AmethystEscapeUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/amethyst-escape/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/amethyst-escape/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/amethyst-escape/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.7.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Amethyst Escape law: `shell rings rotate in fixed increments; connectivity graph is recomputed at angle changes; pearl uses deterministic pocket transitions`. The source of truth is `graph route length and reachable exit proof`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.7.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Amethyst Escape must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are rotate shell, select layer, advance pearl, inspect opening, commit exit. Its unique win predicate is graph route length and reachable exit proof. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 08. Faceted Forge — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G08` • **Source candidate:** `G291` • **Category:** Crystal solids • **Comparative rank:** 8/25 • **Research score:** 93.98/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 84 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Place cleavage planes to split a glowing crystal into target solids. **Signature spectacle:** incandescent mineral interiors opening like a geometric blossom. **Objective:** cut a glowing crystal by placing a bounded number of planes to match target volumes and facet counts. **A failure:** a cut creates disallowed slivers or consumes all remaining cuts. **A victory:** piece-volume vector and face-class multiset match the objective within tolerance.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific finite convex polyhedra partitioning system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag cut-plane rim and depth slider; tap commit for cinematic split. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.8.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** finite convex polyhedra partitioning. **Proposed authoritative law:** planes n·x=d split convex polyhedra; compute oriented intersections; reject degenerate tiny faces; volume from signed tetrahedra. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is convex half-space polytope clipping and exact-oriented face classification with tolerances. **Truth metric:** volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “piece-volume vector and face-class multiset match the objective within tolerance” using `volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “a cut creates disallowed slivers or consumes all remaining cuts”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G08` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct FacetedForgeLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct FacetedForgeState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: cut a glowing crystal by placing a bounded number of planes to match target volumes and facet counts.
// Model: planes n·x=d split convex polyhedra; compute oriented intersections; reject degenerate tiny faces; volume from signed tetrahedra.
// Solver: convex half-space polytope clipping and exact-oriented face classification with tolerances.
```

#### 6.8.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** incandescent mineral interiors opening like a geometric blossom. **Required geometry:** half-space clipping generates per-piece indexed meshes. **Signature shader:** fast SDF cuts reveal incandescent geometric interiors; Beveled polyhedra, faceted signed-distance fields, instanced lattices and faux dispersion. **Palette:** ice glass, ruby, inner amber. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.8.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 84 levels. **Prototype:** simple tetrahedron/cube cuts then constrained multi-piece challenges. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.8.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/FacetedForge/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.8.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `cleavage plane` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “A cut creates disallowed slivers or consumes all remaining cuts”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

A non-applicable test must carry a documented reason, not a silent omission. Platform variants are separate: unit/host is logic proof; iOS 26.5 simulator is compatibility/UI proof; iOS 27.2 simulator is newer SDK behavior proof; actual D1–D3 graphics results come only after Round Two lock.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
#### 6.8.12. Seed-by-seed production-level acceptance and replay contracts
Each numbered stage has *seven mandatory acceptance facets* produced by deterministic test generation. Output below enumerates the complete release catalog: QA should create all indicated artifacts and compare them to `ContentManifest.json`. The same replay witness is consumed by CPU-only unit tests and by simulator gameplay on a selected stratified subset. A stage that lacks one facet is `BLOCKED_CONTENT`, not `PASSED`.

#### 6.8.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** numerical robustness of near-coplanar cuts. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `cleavage plane` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `FacetedForge` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `incandescent mineral interiors opening like a geometric blossom`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `FacetedForge` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `incandescent mineral interiors opening like a geometric blossom`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `FacetedForge` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `incandescent mineral interiors opening like a geometric blossom`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.8.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** numerical robustness of near-coplanar cuts. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `split` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.8.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Faceted Forge
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** cut a glowing crystal by placing a bounded number of planes to match target volumes and facet counts. **CPU domain:** finite convex polyhedra partitioning. **Ground-truth metric:** volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence. **Candidate solver:** convex half-space polytope clipping and exact-oriented face classification with tolerances. The visual identity is incandescent mineral interiors opening like a geometric blossom. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

|---|---|---|
| `Apps/faceted-forge/App/FacetedForgeApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |

| `Apps/faceted-forge/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Domain/FacetedForgeState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Domain/FacetedForgeAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Domain/FacetedForgeRules.swift` | Implement volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Domain/FacetedForgeSolver.swift` | Implement convex half-space polytope clipping and exact-oriented face classification with tolerances | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate planar-clipped convex meshes and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/faceted-forge/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/faceted-forgeUITests/FacetedForgeUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/faceted-forge/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/faceted-forge/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/faceted-forge/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.8.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Faceted Forge law: `planes n·x=d split convex polyhedra; compute oriented intersections; reject degenerate tiny faces; volume from signed tetrahedra`. The source of truth is `volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.8.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Faceted Forge must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are place cut plane, rotate plane, split volume, inspect facet, commit solids. Its unique win predicate is volume conservation and manifold/edge incidence. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 09. Nocturne Garden — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G09` • **Source candidate:** `G368` • **Category:** Shadow construction • **Comparative rank:** 9/25 • **Research score:** 93.96/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 76 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.016667 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Arrange glowing blooms to create a target flower-shaped dark silhouette. **Signature spectacle:** black botanical silhouettes climbing through luminous pearlescent mist. **Objective:** arrange procedurally grown flowers so their projected shadows form a target silhouette. **A failure:** shadow area leaks into prohibited outline regions. **A victory:** target mask IoU exceeds requirement and no penalty-region pixels exceed budget.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific silhouette composition system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag stems, pinch scale, slide sun elevation; silhouette preview as exact diagnostic. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.9.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** silhouette composition. **Proposed authoritative law:** orthographic projected polygon union rasterized into a deterministic low-resolution mask; quality measured by IoU plus boundary deviation. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.016667 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is grid-snapped candidate placements with stencil overlap and shape-distance scoring. **Truth metric:** mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “target mask IoU exceeds requirement and no penalty-region pixels exceed budget” using `mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “shadow area leaks into prohibited outline regions”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.

```swift
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct NocturneGardenState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: arrange procedurally grown flowers so their projected shadows form a target silhouette.
// Model: orthographic projected polygon union rasterized into a deterministic low-resolution mask; quality measured by IoU plus boundary deviation.
// Solver: grid-snapped candidate placements with stencil overlap and shape-distance scoring.
```

#### 6.9.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** black botanical silhouettes climbing through luminous pearlescent mist. **Required geometry:** L-system stems, leaf polygons and projected shadow mesh. **Signature shader:** deep black botanical shadows on colored mist planes; Procedural solids, CPU polygonal 3D shadow projections, soft shadow approximation. **Palette:** midnight blue, lantern coral and parchment gold. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.9.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 76 levels. **Prototype:** 60 silhouette challenges with 8 flower grammars. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

#### 6.9.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/NocturneGarden/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.9.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `bloom` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Shadow area leaks into prohibited outline regions”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

##### R2-G09-01: Playable rule kernel

Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
