#### 6.9.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** silhouette-based objectives can become repetitive; design layered flower grammar combinations. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `bloom` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `NocturneGarden` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black botanical silhouettes climbing through luminous pearlescent mist`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `NocturneGarden` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black botanical silhouettes climbing through luminous pearlescent mist`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `NocturneGarden` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black botanical silhouettes climbing through luminous pearlescent mist`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.9.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** silhouette-based objectives can become repetitive; design layered flower grammar combinations. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `arrange` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.9.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Nocturne Garden
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** arrange procedurally grown flowers so their projected shadows form a target silhouette. **CPU domain:** silhouette composition. **Ground-truth metric:** mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy. **Candidate solver:** grid-snapped candidate placements with stencil overlap and shape-distance scoring. The visual identity is black botanical silhouettes climbing through luminous pearlescent mist. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

| `Packages/Games/nocturne-garden/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate L-system flower meshes and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |

| `Packages/Games/nocturne-garden/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/nocturne-garden/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/nocturne-gardenUITests/NocturneGardenUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/nocturne-garden/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/nocturne-garden/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/nocturne-garden/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.9.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Nocturne Garden law: `orthographic projected polygon union rasterized into a deterministic low-resolution mask; quality measured by IoU plus boundary deviation`. The source of truth is `mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.
| Test ID | Scope / fixture | Action sequence or fault injection | Expected authoritative oracle | Visual and accessibility expectation | Evidence file / gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-G09-QA-001` | **Truth and state transitions: fresh install and zero-history start**, seed `1f4290021d42983e`; Legal control changes exactly the specified authoritative model and no shader value can create a win. | Load planned level 035; issue legal `commit shadow` command at a canonical tick; then issue deliberately illegal command crossing `similar-looking color-only clue` condition. | CPU `mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy` equals expected fixture / reject reason for `deterministic projected silhouette`; canonical hash and action count match the versioned golden or logged witness. A missing witness means BLOCKED, never PASS. | `shadow projection on ground quad` visibly reflects the true state without being a victory oracle; `similar-looking color-only clue` must produce an explicit understandable UI state, not flicker, an ad, or an infinite spinner. | `docs/test-reports/round2/nocturne-garden/qa/001.json` with command, scheme, runtime, binary hash and result bundle |

#### 6.9.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Nocturne Garden must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are place stem, adjust bloom pose, aim moonlight, trim leaf, commit shadow. Its unique win predicate is mask intersection-over-union and contour Hausdorff proxy. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 10. Backwards Aurora — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G10` • **Source candidate:** `G451` • **Category:** Temporal puzzles • **Comparative rank:** 10/25 • **Research score:** 93.96/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 76 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Correct a hidden signal by reversing sections of an auroral wave. **Signature spectacle:** rivers of aurora folding backward through time in synchronized waves. **Objective:** reverse selected intervals of a flowing aurora so corrupted waveform sections reconstruct an original target. **A failure:** seams exceed curvature limits after reversing. **A victory:** reconstructed waveform matches target checkpoints and seam limits.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific piecewise reversible wave field system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.
#### 6.10.1. Player journey and minute-by-minute first play

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** tap segment ends, swipe the interval to reverse, timeline freeze preview. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.10.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** piecewise reversible wave field. **Proposed authoritative law:** signal samples in signed fixed precision; interval reversal must preserve seam continuity and bounded curvature. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is interval dynamic programming over reversible wave segments and endpoint continuity constraints. **Truth metric:** normalized signal edit distance and continuity.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “reconstructed waveform matches target checkpoints and seam limits” using `normalized signal edit distance and continuity`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “seams exceed curvature limits after reversing”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G10` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct BackwardsAuroraLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct BackwardsAuroraState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: reverse selected intervals of a flowing aurora so corrupted waveform sections reconstruct an original target.
// Model: signal samples in signed fixed precision; interval reversal must preserve seam continuity and bounded curvature.
// Solver: interval dynamic programming over reversible wave segments and endpoint continuity constraints.
```

#### 6.10.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** rivers of aurora folding backward through time in synchronized waves. **Required geometry:** tessellated temporal ribbon with direction-coded pulses. **Signature shader:** auroral ribbons fold backward along procedural timelines; Deterministic timeline buffers, ghost trails, reversible deformation shaders. **Palette:** deep ocean cyan, pale lilac, midnight. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.10.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 76 levels. **Prototype:** 70 ordered interval reversal and phase-seam puzzles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.10.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/BackwardsAurora/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.10.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `wave interval` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `normalized signal edit distance and continuity`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Seams exceed curvature limits after reversing”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.10.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** too similar visually to Aurora Loom; enforce puzzle-first temporal identity and unique visual style. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `wave interval` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** normalized signal edit distance and continuity stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `BackwardsAurora` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `rivers of aurora folding backward through time in synchronized waves`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `BackwardsAurora` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `rivers of aurora folding backward through time in synchronized waves`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `BackwardsAurora` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `rivers of aurora folding backward through time in synchronized waves`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.10.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** too similar visually to Aurora Loom; enforce puzzle-first temporal identity and unique visual style. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `reverse` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.10.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Backwards Aurora
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** reverse selected intervals of a flowing aurora so corrupted waveform sections reconstruct an original target. **CPU domain:** piecewise reversible wave field. **Ground-truth metric:** normalized signal edit distance and continuity. **Candidate solver:** interval dynamic programming over reversible wave segments and endpoint continuity constraints. The visual identity is rivers of aurora folding backward through time in synchronized waves. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.10.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/backwards-aurora/App/BackwardsAuroraApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/backwards-aurora/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/backwards-aurora/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/backwards-aurora/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/backwards-aurora/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/backwards-aurora/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Domain/BackwardsAuroraState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Domain/BackwardsAuroraAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Domain/BackwardsAuroraRules.swift` | Implement normalized signal edit distance and continuity | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Domain/BackwardsAuroraSolver.swift` | Implement interval dynamic programming over reversible wave segments and endpoint continuity constraints | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate spectral strip mesh and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/backwards-aurora/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/backwards-auroraUITests/BackwardsAuroraUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/backwards-aurora/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/backwards-aurora/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/backwards-aurora/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

#### 6.10.17. Architectural decision ledger — explicit choices and failure semantics
| ID | Decision to implement | Why this is required for this particular game | Verification before acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-G10-ADR-01` | **Canonical state and serialization.** Define a stable versioned schema. Separate player controls, discrete puzzle objects, authored level parameters, solver witness and visual-only particle state. | In **Backwards Aurora**, `bounded interval reversal` is the rule-level requirement while `spectral strip mesh` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against off-by-one reversal window; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `normalized signal edit distance and continuity` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G10-ADR-02` | **Fixed-step scheduling.** Use integer tick count and a bounded accumulator; cap accumulated elapsed time after suspension; never use display refresh delta as a victory predicate. | In **Backwards Aurora**, `continuity at cuts` is the rule-level requirement while `time-reversal shader sweeps` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against mismatched endpoint derivative; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `normalized signal edit distance and continuity` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G10-ADR-03` | **Control discretization.** Quantize the five listed gestures into distinct command cases with stable IDs; deterministic rounding rules must be identical in simulator and device builds. | In **Backwards Aurora**, `signal edit distance` is the rule-level requirement while `source/target waveform ribbon` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against ambiguous undo; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `normalized signal edit distance and continuity` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G10-ADR-04` | **World and camera coordinates.** Adopt right-handed world units, explicit view/projection matrices, stable near/far planes and reversible touch-to-world mapping for every selectable handle. | In **Backwards Aurora**, `reversible history` is the rule-level requirement while `seam cues` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against apparent reverse without data change; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `normalized signal edit distance and continuity` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G10-ADR-05` | **Puzzle invariants.** Centralize source-of-truth checks on the CPU; each accepted action either produces a new consistent state or returns an explicit typed rejection. | In **Backwards Aurora**, `target reconstruction threshold` is the rule-level requirement while `layered atmospheric gradient` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against floating-point drift; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `normalized signal edit distance and continuity` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.10.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Backwards Aurora law: `signal samples in signed fixed precision; interval reversal must preserve seam continuity and bounded curvature`. The source of truth is `normalized signal edit distance and continuity`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.10.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Backwards Aurora must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are select interval, reverse signal, splice segments, align waveform, validate reconstruction. Its unique win predicate is normalized signal edit distance and continuity. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 11. Echo Cartographer — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G11` • **Source candidate:** `G181` • **Category:** Logic and patterns • **Comparative rank:** 11/25 • **Research score:** 93.91/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 90 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Touch to emit a pulse, mark reflected obstacles, locate hidden beacons; seeded room generator. **Signature spectacle:** dark temples briefly crystallizing into wireframe from expanding cyan light. **Objective:** emit timed sonar pulses to identify invisible walls and locate hidden beacons with limited energy. **A failure:** energy is exhausted without locating all beacons. **A victory:** every beacon triangulated and tapped inside a spatial tolerance.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific reflective line-of-sight chamber mapping system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** tap to emit pulse; triangulate via dragging markers; rotate 3D camera. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.11.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** reflective line-of-sight chamber mapping. **Proposed authoritative law:** raycast wave returns with path-length delay; echoes based on static convex segments; deterministic time-of-flight per beam. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is grid chamber generator with connected-component and unique beacon inference proof. **Truth metric:** ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “every beacon triangulated and tapped inside a spatial tolerance” using `ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “energy is exhausted without locating all beacons”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G11` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct EchoCartographerLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct EchoCartographerState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: emit timed sonar pulses to identify invisible walls and locate hidden beacons with limited energy.
// Model: raycast wave returns with path-length delay; echoes based on static convex segments; deterministic time-of-flight per beam.
// Solver: grid chamber generator with connected-component and unique beacon inference proof.
```

#### 6.11.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** dark temples briefly crystallizing into wireframe from expanding cyan light. **Required geometry:** SDF primitives plus instanced wireframe edge strips. **Signature shader:** Signed-distance chamber topology, instanced wireframe surfaces, expanding normal-aware echo waves. **Palette:** abyss black, sonar mint and opal. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.11.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 90 levels. **Prototype:** 20 curated sonar rooms then generated obstacle topologies. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.
**Per-level planned content manifest.** Every line below is a *requirement for generating and certifying an individual stage*, not a statement that the level currently exists. Values are stable derived design seeds/metadata; actual target parameters and solver witness must be generated and stored at build time.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.11.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/EchoCartographer/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.11.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `echo` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Energy is exhausted without locating all beacons”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.11.9. Explicit VisualCore shared-feature dependencies
This game requires the following Stage Two features before app implementation begins; select only the features not already satisfied by audited Stage One components:
- `R2-F01` — Round 1 evidence & reproducible baseline audit. Reference its verified API in `Apps/EchoCartographer/Rendering/EchoCartographerSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F02` — VisualCore public API compatibility and renderer capability probing. Reference its verified API in `Apps/EchoCartographer/Rendering/EchoCartographerSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F03` — Numerical foundations and deterministic seeded scene time. Reference its verified API in `Apps/EchoCartographer/Rendering/EchoCartographerSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F04` — GPU resource ownership and pipeline lifetime. Reference its verified API in `Apps/EchoCartographer/Rendering/EchoCartographerSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F05` — Procedural mesh compiler and mesh validation. Reference its verified API in `Apps/EchoCartographer/Rendering/EchoCartographerSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.

#### 6.11.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** 3D readability and confusion between true and reflected echoes. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `echo` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `EchoCartographer` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `dark temples briefly crystallizing into wireframe from expanding cyan light`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `EchoCartographer` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `dark temples briefly crystallizing into wireframe from expanding cyan light`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `EchoCartographer` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `dark temples briefly crystallizing into wireframe from expanding cyan light`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.11.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** 3D readability and confusion between true and reflected echoes. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `pulse` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.11.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Echo Cartographer
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** emit timed sonar pulses to identify invisible walls and locate hidden beacons with limited energy. **CPU domain:** reflective line-of-sight chamber mapping. **Ground-truth metric:** ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error. **Candidate solver:** grid chamber generator with connected-component and unique beacon inference proof. The visual identity is dark temples briefly crystallizing into wireframe from expanding cyan light. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.11.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/echo-cartographer/App/EchoCartographerApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/echo-cartographer/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/echo-cartographer/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/echo-cartographer/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/echo-cartographer/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/echo-cartographer/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Domain/EchoCartographerState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Domain/EchoCartographerAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Domain/EchoCartographerRules.swift` | Implement ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Domain/EchoCartographerSolver.swift` | Implement grid chamber generator with connected-component and unique beacon inference proof | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate expanding sonar wavefront shells and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/echo-cartographer/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/echo-cartographerUITests/EchoCartographerUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/echo-cartographer/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/echo-cartographer/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/echo-cartographer/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.11.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Echo Cartographer law: `raycast wave returns with path-length delay; echoes based on static convex segments; deterministic time-of-flight per beam`. The source of truth is `ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.11.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Echo Cartographer must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are send pulse, mark obstacle, estimate echo, triangulate beacon, commit map. Its unique win predicate is ray travel distance agreement and beacon localization error. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 12. Harmonic Bridges — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G12` • **Source candidate:** `G217` • **Category:** Acoustic geometry • **Comparative rank:** 12/25 • **Research score:** 93.81/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 82 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Tune suspended strings so their resonances solidify walkable bridges. **Signature spectacle:** strings swelling into translucent glowing architecture as they find resonance. **Objective:** tune suspended strings until stable antinodes create connected walkways between islands. **A failure:** bridge breaks during a crossing-window step. **A victory:** start to goal reachability sustained for required window.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific standing-wave bridge formation system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** pluck to audition frequency, drag tuning peg, tap freeze to test walkway. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.12.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** standing-wave bridge formation. **Proposed authoritative law:** y(x,t)=sum A_n sin(n*pi*x/L)*cos(omega_n*t+phi_n); solidity threshold from time-averaged envelope. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is discrete rational string-mode search with graph edge existence and reachability. **Truth metric:** mode amplitude envelope and bridge graph connectivity.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “start to goal reachability sustained for required window” using `mode amplitude envelope and bridge graph connectivity`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “bridge breaks during a crossing-window step”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G12` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct HarmonicBridgesLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct HarmonicBridgesState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: tune suspended strings until stable antinodes create connected walkways between islands.
// Model: y(x,t)=sum A_n sin(n*pi*x/L)*cos(omega_n*t+phi_n); solidity threshold from time-averaged envelope.
// Solver: discrete rational string-mode search with graph edge existence and reachability.
```

#### 6.12.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** strings swelling into translucent glowing architecture as they find resonance. **Required geometry:** swept strings and radial wave-shell strip meshes. **Signature shader:** oscillating wave membranes stretch between crystalline anchors; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals. **Palette:** warm copper, cyan membranes and mist violet. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.12.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 82 levels. **Prototype:** 2-string, then 5-string bridge mazes with harmonic locks. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

#### 6.12.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/HarmonicBridges/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.12.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `string` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `mode amplitude envelope and bridge graph connectivity`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Bridge breaks during a crossing-window step”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
