#### 6.19.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** large swarm update CPU load; use deterministic low-count CPU boids with GPU instancing. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `swimmer` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** swarm density distribution and pattern connectivity stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `MicroscopicAurora` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `bioluminescent protozoa making aurora-like ribbons under a microscope`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `MicroscopicAurora` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `bioluminescent protozoa making aurora-like ribbons under a microscope`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `MicroscopicAurora` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `bioluminescent protozoa making aurora-like ribbons under a microscope`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.19.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** large swarm update CPU load; use deterministic low-count CPU boids with GPU instancing. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `herd` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.19.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Microscopic Aurora
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** control a small field of magnetic swimmers so their luminous trails compose target living patterns. **CPU domain:** deterministic magnetic boid swarms. **Ground-truth metric:** swarm density distribution and pattern connectivity. **Candidate solver:** low-dimensional field strength search with seeded boid simulator and shape-loss evaluation. The visual identity is bioluminescent protozoa making aurora-like ribbons under a microscope. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.19.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Microscopic Aurora law: `boids use bounded separation/alignment/cohesion accelerations plus magnetic curl field; stable fixed-step integration`. The source of truth is `swarm density distribution and pattern connectivity`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.19.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Microscopic Aurora must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are place magnetic pole, tune field, release swimmers, record trail, commit organism shape. Its unique win predicate is swarm density distribution and pattern connectivity. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 20. Mushroom Weather — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G20` • **Source candidate:** `G414` • **Category:** Micro ecosystems • **Comparative rank:** 20/25 • **Research score:** 93.04/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 76 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.016667 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Arrange fungi to create a stable forest humidity network. **Signature spectacle:** glowing umbrella caps breathing droplets into a midnight miniature forest. **Objective:** arrange fungi and adjust microclimate to maintain stable humidity lanes between mushroom colonies. **A failure:** sensitive colony dries out or mold saturation exceeds upper bound. **A victory:** all target colonies sustain preferred humidity band for T cycles.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific localized moisture diffusion and growth system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag spore pods, open or close canopy vents, shift moonlight intensity. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.20.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** localized moisture diffusion and growth. **Proposed authoritative law:** humidity_{t+1}=humidity_t+D*laplacian*dt - evaporation + release; growth triggered by time-integrated thresholds. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.016667 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is grid diffusion with bounded evapotranspiration and reachability checks. **Truth metric:** humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all target colonies sustain preferred humidity band for T cycles” using `humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “sensitive colony dries out or mold saturation exceeds upper bound”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.

```swift
}
struct MushroomWeatherState: Codable {

    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,

// Game objective: arrange fungi and adjust microclimate to maintain stable humidity lanes between mushroom colonies.

// Solver: grid diffusion with bounded evapotranspiration and reachability checks.
```

#### 6.20.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** glowing umbrella caps breathing droplets into a midnight miniature forest. **Required geometry:** procedural lathed stalks and SDF mushroom caps. **Signature shader:** translucent mushroom caps sparkle with moisture gradients; L-system miniature flora, deterministic boids, bioluminescence and simple water planes. **Palette:** fern jade, amber spores and deep blue. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.20.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 76 levels. **Prototype:** 70 humidity-routing puzzles with 5 procedural cap species. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.20.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/MushroomWeather/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.20.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `fungus` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Sensitive colony dries out or mold saturation exceeds upper bound”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
#### 6.20.12. Seed-by-seed production-level acceptance and replay contracts
Each numbered stage has *seven mandatory acceptance facets* produced by deterministic test generation. Output below enumerates the complete release catalog: QA should create all indicated artifacts and compare them to `ContentManifest.json`. The same replay witness is consumed by CPU-only unit tests and by simulator gameplay on a selected stratified subset. A stage that lacks one facet is `BLOCKED_CONTENT`, not `PASSED`.

#### 6.20.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** must avoid hand-built natural assets; all plants use grammar meshes. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `fungus` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `MushroomWeather` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `glowing umbrella caps breathing droplets into a midnight miniature forest`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `MushroomWeather` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `glowing umbrella caps breathing droplets into a midnight miniature forest`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `MushroomWeather` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `glowing umbrella caps breathing droplets into a midnight miniature forest`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.20.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** must avoid hand-built natural assets; all plants use grammar meshes. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `cultivate` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.20.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Mushroom Weather
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** arrange fungi and adjust microclimate to maintain stable humidity lanes between mushroom colonies. **CPU domain:** localized moisture diffusion and growth. **Ground-truth metric:** humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals. **Candidate solver:** grid diffusion with bounded evapotranspiration and reachability checks. The visual identity is glowing umbrella caps breathing droplets into a midnight miniature forest. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.20.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Mushroom Weather law: `humidity_{t+1}=humidity_t+D*laplacian*dt - evaporation + release; growth triggered by time-integrated thresholds`. The source of truth is `humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.20.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Mushroom Weather must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are place fungus, adjust mist vent, open canopy, route humidity, commit season. Its unique win predicate is humidity conservation with source/sink ledger and colony survival intervals. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 21. Binary Gardens — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G21` • **Source candidate:** `G249` • **Category:** Orbital dynamics • **Comparative rank:** 21/25 • **Research score:** 93.0/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 81 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Balance twin stars to keep orbiting flower worlds within a light zone. **Signature spectacle:** two suns painting crossing sunrise bands over tiny flowering spheres. **Objective:** adjust two stellar orbits to maintain tiny garden planets inside a moving illumination window. **A failure:** world receives lethal low/high flux for too many ticks. **A victory:** each garden world has stable illumination window across a full cycle.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific toy circumbinary habitability simulation system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag star distance rings, tilt orbit plane, inspect each miniature world. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.21.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** toy circumbinary habitability simulation. **Proposed authoritative law:** approximate flux=sum luminosity_i/max(r_i^2,r_min^2); orbit curves analytic; plants respond to integrated flux bands. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is bounded coupled-orbit parameter sweep with sampling of received flux. **Truth metric:** per-world integrated normalized flux and survival.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “each garden world has stable illumination window across a full cycle” using `per-world integrated normalized flux and survival`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “world receives lethal low/high flux for too many ticks”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift

    let objectiveID: String

    let maxActions: Int

    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct BinaryGardensState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: adjust two stellar orbits to maintain tiny garden planets inside a moving illumination window.
// Model: approximate flux=sum luminosity_i/max(r_i^2,r_min^2); orbit curves analytic; plants respond to integrated flux bands.
// Solver: bounded coupled-orbit parameter sweep with sampling of received flux.
```

#### 6.21.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** two suns painting crossing sunrise bands over tiny flowering spheres. **Required geometry:** cube-sphere planet mesh and shader-only seasonal banding. **Signature shader:** twin light discs and procedural luminous planet ecologies; Numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields. **Palette:** warm vermilion, ice blue and mint world. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.21.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 81 levels. **Prototype:** one-world tutorial through three-world circumbinary puzzles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.21.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/BinaryGardens/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.21.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `twin star` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `per-world integrated normalized flux and survival`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “World receives lethal low/high flux for too many ticks”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.21.10. Feature-by-feature complete Spec Kit prompts for this game
**Feature numbering:** `R2-G21-01` through `R2-G21-10` (globally unique within Stage Two), one spec folder per feature. **Activation:** confirm active `.specify/feature.json` points at the expected folder before each invocation. **Sequence:** specify, clarify, plan, checklist, tasks, analyze, implement, converge. Read generated outputs and correct blocking issues between steps. The prompts below are literal messages for **Claude Desktop Code**; none is a Terminal command. *Every implement must be followed by actual tests and converge*.
##### R2-G21-01: Playable rule kernel
**Spec directory:** `specs/501-binary-gardens-playable-rule-kernel/` • **Functional requirement:** Implement deterministic state transition and exact win/failure evaluation. **Unique game objective:** adjust two stellar orbits to maintain tiny garden planets inside a moving illumination window. **Domain algorithm:** approximate flux=sum luminosity_i/max(r_i^2,r_min^2); orbit curves analytic; plants respond to integrated flux bands. **Reference solver:** bounded coupled-orbit parameter sweep with sampling of received flux. **Required Stage Two dependencies:** R2-F01, R2-F02, R2-F03, R2-F04, R2-F05, R2-F06, R2-F07, R2-F15, R2-F19, R2-F21, R2-F22, R2-F23, R2-F24, R2-F25, R2-F26, R2-F27, R2-F28, R2-F29, R2-F30, R2-F31, R2-F32, R2-F33, R2-F34.
**Proof obligation:** demonstrate this slice works in `BinaryGardens` and does not break any unrelated existing app. All logic path tests use the stored seed/witness; render slice tests use the existing ANGLE-backed shader host. Device-specific proof is **only planned here** until after all 25 new game targets pass simulator lock.
```text
/speckit-specify Define production requirements for R2-G21-01 Binary Gardens: Playable rule kernel. Purpose: Implement deterministic state transition and exact win/failure evaluation. Prerequisites: R2-F01; R2-F02; R2-F03; R2-F04; R2-F05; R2-F06; R2-F07; R2-F15; R2-F19; R2-F21; R2-F22; R2-F23; R2-F24; R2-F25; R2-F26; R2-F27; R2-F28; R2-F29; R2-F30; R2-F31; R2-F32; R2-F33; R2-F34. ##### R2-G21-10: Device automation preparation
```
**Spec directory:** `specs/510-binary-gardens-device-automation-preparation/` • **Functional requirement:** Build automation runner and acceptance contract but do not launch a device yet. **Unique game objective:** adjust two stellar orbits to maintain tiny garden planets inside a moving illumination window. **Domain algorithm:** approximate flux=sum luminosity_i/max(r_i^2,r_min^2); orbit curves analytic; plants respond to integrated flux bands. **Reference solver:** bounded coupled-orbit parameter sweep with sampling of received flux. **Required Stage Two dependencies:** R2-F01, R2-F02, R2-F03, R2-F04, R2-F05, R2-F06, R2-F07, R2-F15, R2-F19, R2-F21, R2-F22, R2-F23, R2-F24, R2-F25, R2-F26, R2-F27, R2-F28, R2-F29, R2-F30, R2-F31, R2-F32, R2-F33, R2-F34.

#### 6.21.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** do not present astrobiological correctness; physics is explicit toy model. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `twin star` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** per-world integrated normalized flux and survival stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `BinaryGardens` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `two suns painting crossing sunrise bands over tiny flowering spheres`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `BinaryGardens` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `two suns painting crossing sunrise bands over tiny flowering spheres`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `BinaryGardens` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `two suns painting crossing sunrise bands over tiny flowering spheres`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.21.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** do not present astrobiological correctness; physics is explicit toy model. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `balance` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.21.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Binary Gardens
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** adjust two stellar orbits to maintain tiny garden planets inside a moving illumination window. **CPU domain:** toy circumbinary habitability simulation. **Ground-truth metric:** per-world integrated normalized flux and survival. **Candidate solver:** bounded coupled-orbit parameter sweep with sampling of received flux. The visual identity is two suns painting crossing sunrise bands over tiny flowering spheres. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate dual solar corona sprites and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |

| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |

| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/binary-gardens/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/binary-gardensUITests/BinaryGardensUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/binary-gardens/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/binary-gardens/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/binary-gardens/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

#### 6.21.17. Architectural decision ledger — explicit choices and failure semantics
| ID | Decision to implement | Why this is required for this particular game | Verification before acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-G21-ADR-01` | **Canonical state and serialization.** Define a stable versioned schema. Separate player controls, discrete puzzle objects, authored level parameters, solver witness and visual-only particle state. | In **Binary Gardens**, `bounded inverse-square flux` is the rule-level requirement while `dual solar corona sprites` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against divide by near-zero radius; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `per-world integrated normalized flux and survival` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |
| `R2-G21-ADR-02` | **Fixed-step scheduling.** Use integer tick count and a bounded accumulator; cap accumulated elapsed time after suspension; never use display refresh delta as a victory predicate. | In **Binary Gardens**, `circumbinary orbit phase` is the rule-level requirement while `cube-sphere garden planets` supplies the procedural visual vocabulary. Specifically guard against numerical runaway flux; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `per-world integrated normalized flux and survival` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |

Specifically guard against false realistic astrophysics claim; it cannot be concealed by camera changes, visual polish, or a waiver. | Add a failing fixture first, use `per-world integrated normalized flux and survival` as the authoritative oracle when applicable, rerun host and simulator checks, record exact command+result SHA and create a formal ADR for any changed contract. |

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.21.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Binary Gardens law: `approximate flux=sum luminosity_i/max(r_i^2,r_min^2); orbit curves analytic; plants respond to integrated flux bands`. The source of truth is `per-world integrated normalized flux and survival`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.21.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Binary Gardens must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are phase twin stars, adjust orbit, set luminosity, watch world, commit light window. Its unique win predicate is per-world integrated normalized flux and survival. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 22. Mycelium Architect — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G22` • **Source candidate:** `G276` • **Category:** Organic growth • **Comparative rank:** 22/25 • **Research score:** 92.91/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 84 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.016667 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Feed fungal networks so glowing veins form a target graph around rocks. **Signature spectacle:** organic veins pulsing like a starlit subterranean city. **Objective:** feed nutrient sources so living luminous fungal veins grow into a specified network without crossing toxins. **A failure:** network enters toxic volume or exceeds nutrient budget. **A victory:** required terminals connected with at most specified branch weight.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific branching graph flow optimization system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** place nutrients and blockers, advance growth pulses, undo edits. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.22.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** branching graph flow optimization. **Proposed authoritative law:** each tip chooses max nutrient-gradient direction minus curvature and obstacle penalties; graph cap 2048 nodes. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.016667 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is graph shortest path plus deterministic branching-growth heuristic and target topology check. **Truth metric:** root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “required terminals connected with at most specified branch weight” using `root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “network enters toxic volume or exceeds nutrient budget”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift

    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct MyceliumArchitectState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: feed nutrient sources so living luminous fungal veins grow into a specified network without crossing toxins.

// Solver: graph shortest path plus deterministic branching-growth heuristic and target topology check.
```

#### 6.22.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** organic veins pulsing like a starlit subterranean city. **Required geometry:** instanced tapered cylinder branch segments and procedural cap mushrooms. **Signature shader:** recursive hyphae bloom under translucent luminous caps; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials. **Palette:** emerald, copper and violet roots. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.22.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 84 levels. **Prototype:** 80 network puzzles across procedural soil volumes. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.22.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/MyceliumArchitect/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.22.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `hypha` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Network enters toxic volume or exceeds nutrient budget”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.22.9. Explicit VisualCore shared-feature dependencies
This game requires the following Stage Two features before app implementation begins; select only the features not already satisfied by audited Stage One components:
- `R2-F01` — Round 1 evidence & reproducible baseline audit. Reference its verified API in `Apps/MyceliumArchitect/Rendering/MyceliumArchitectSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F02` — VisualCore public API compatibility and renderer capability probing. Reference its verified API in `Apps/MyceliumArchitect/Rendering/MyceliumArchitectSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F03` — Numerical foundations and deterministic seeded scene time. Reference its verified API in `Apps/MyceliumArchitect/Rendering/MyceliumArchitectSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.
- `R2-F04` — GPU resource ownership and pipeline lifetime. Reference its verified API in `Apps/MyceliumArchitect/Rendering/MyceliumArchitectSceneAdapter.swift` or the pure logic package as appropriate.

Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.

#### 6.22.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** visually organic but too close to reference PRNG metaphors; gameplay originality must remain distinct. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `hypha` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `MyceliumArchitect` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `organic veins pulsing like a starlit subterranean city`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `MyceliumArchitect` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `organic veins pulsing like a starlit subterranean city`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `MyceliumArchitect` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `organic veins pulsing like a starlit subterranean city`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.22.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** visually organic but too close to reference PRNG metaphors; gameplay originality must remain distinct. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `grow` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.22.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Mycelium Architect
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** feed nutrient sources so living luminous fungal veins grow into a specified network without crossing toxins. **CPU domain:** branching graph flow optimization. **Ground-truth metric:** root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits. **Candidate solver:** graph shortest path plus deterministic branching-growth heuristic and target topology check. The visual identity is organic veins pulsing like a starlit subterranean city. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.22.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/mycelium-architect/App/MyceliumArchitectApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/mycelium-architect/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/mycelium-architect/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/mycelium-architect/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/mycelium-architect/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/mycelium-architect/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Domain/MyceliumArchitectState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Domain/MyceliumArchitectAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Domain/MyceliumArchitectRules.swift` | Implement root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Domain/MyceliumArchitectSolver.swift` | Implement graph shortest path plus deterministic branching-growth heuristic and target topology check | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate graph-to-tube hyphae meshes and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/mycelium-architect/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/mycelium-architectUITests/MyceliumArchitectUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/mycelium-architect/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/mycelium-architect/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/mycelium-architect/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.22.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Mycelium Architect law: `each tip chooses max nutrient-gradient direction minus curvature and obstacle penalties; graph cap 2048 nodes`. The source of truth is `root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.
