#### 6.22.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Mycelium Architect must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are place nutrient, seed filament, block toxin, steer growth, commit graph. Its unique win predicate is root-to-terminal connectivity, total branch cost and forbidden-zone hits. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 23. Erosion Painter — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G23` • **Source candidate:** `G321` • **Category:** Terrain alchemy • **Comparative rank:** 23/25 • **Research score:** 92.9/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 76 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.016667 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Raise and lower terrain to coax rain into carving a target canyon. **Signature spectacle:** mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather. **Objective:** sculpt hills and rainfall patterns until erosion carves a prescribed canyon network. **A failure:** protected ridges disappear or target region floods. **A victory:** drainage graph and canyon height profile match target within tolerances.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific heightfield erosion with capped sediment flow system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** brush height with two-finger scale, tap cloud cells, run/pause epochs. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.23.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** heightfield erosion with capped sediment flow. **Proposed authoritative law:** water flux obeys local downhill differences; erode min(k*flow, sediment capacity); deposition restores sediment; clamps conserve material ledger. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.016667 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is iterative heightfield transport with deterministic hydraulic approximations and seed replay. **Truth metric:** mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “drainage graph and canyon height profile match target within tolerances” using `mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “protected ridges disappear or target region floods”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.

}

    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]

    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}

#### 6.23.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather. **Required geometry:** adaptive tessellated heightfield and flowing shader streaks. **Signature shader:** procedural heightfields channel glowing water and sediment; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. **Palette:** sunset vermilion, turquoise rain and violet shadow. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.23.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 76 levels. **Prototype:** 12 tutorial basins then terrain-generator challenges. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.23.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/ErosionPainter/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.23.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `terrain brush` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Protected ridges disappear or target region floods”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
#### 6.23.12. Seed-by-seed production-level acceptance and replay contracts
Each numbered stage has *seven mandatory acceptance facets* produced by deterministic test generation. Output below enumerates the complete release catalog: QA should create all indicated artifacts and compare them to `ContentManifest.json`. The same replay witness is consumed by CPU-only unit tests and by simulator gameplay on a selected stratified subset. A stage that lacks one facet is `BLOCKED_CONTENT`, not `PASSED`.

#### 6.23.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** thermal/load of repeated high-res terrain; simulate low-res and render adaptively. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `terrain brush` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `ErosionPainter` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `ErosionPainter` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `ErosionPainter` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.23.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** thermal/load of repeated high-res terrain; simulate low-res and render adaptively. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `sculpt` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.23.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Erosion Painter
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** sculpt hills and rainfall patterns until erosion carves a prescribed canyon network. **CPU domain:** heightfield erosion with capped sediment flow. **Ground-truth metric:** mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph. **Candidate solver:** iterative heightfield transport with deterministic hydraulic approximations and seed replay. The visual identity is mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |

| `Apps/erosion-painter/App/ErosionPainterApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |

| `Apps/erosion-painter/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/erosion-painter/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Domain/ErosionPainterState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Domain/ErosionPainterAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Domain/ErosionPainterRules.swift` | Implement mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Domain/ErosionPainterSolver.swift` | Implement iterative heightfield transport with deterministic hydraulic approximations and seed replay | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate tessellated heightfield and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/erosion-painter/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/erosion-painterUITests/ErosionPainterUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/erosion-painter/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/erosion-painter/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/erosion-painter/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.23.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Erosion Painter law: `water flux obeys local downhill differences; erode min(k*flow, sediment capacity); deposition restores sediment; clamps conserve material ledger`. The source of truth is `mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

After lock execute app×D1, app×D2, app×D3 in the portfolio-level contiguous device order; do not substitute simulator exports.

#### 6.23.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Erosion Painter must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are raise terrain, lower terrain, place rain, dig spillway, simulate erosion. Its unique win predicate is mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 24. Crystal Quarry — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G24` • **Source candidate:** `G334` • **Category:** Terrain alchemy • **Comparative rank:** 24/25 • **Research score:** 92.9/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 86 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Choose fracture paths to reveal a target gem network in rock. **Signature spectacle:** black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations. **Objective:** choose break lines to expose a hidden gem network in a procedural rock body. **A failure:** critical gem is destroyed or energy limit reached. **A victory:** all target seam nodes exposed with host rock stability preserved.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific terrain-contained voxel fracture network system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag guided cleavage stroke, tap inspect mineral glow, rotate core. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.24.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** terrain-contained voxel fracture network. **Proposed authoritative law:** rock consists of bounded convex chunks from deterministic Voronoi seeds; split along known planes, not dynamic brittle FEM. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints. **Truth metric:** reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all target seam nodes exposed with host rock stability preserved” using `reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “critical gem is destroyed or energy limit reached”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift

    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct CrystalQuarryState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: choose break lines to expose a hidden gem network in a procedural rock body.
// Model: rock consists of bounded convex chunks from deterministic Voronoi seeds; split along known planes, not dynamic brittle FEM.
// Solver: seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints.
```

#### 6.24.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations. **Required geometry:** deterministic Voronoi chunk meshes with internal seam shader. **Signature shader:** glowing mineral seams emerge through geometric stone fractures; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. **Palette:** slate obsidian, emerald and molten rose. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.24.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 86 levels. **Prototype:** graded mineral clusters and multi-step exposure puzzles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.24.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/CrystalQuarry/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.24.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `fracture` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Critical gem is destroyed or energy limit reached”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.24.10. Feature-by-feature complete Spec Kit prompts for this game
**Feature numbering:** `R2-G24-01` through `R2-G24-10` (globally unique within Stage Two), one spec folder per feature. **Activation:** confirm active `.specify/feature.json` points at the expected folder before each invocation. **Sequence:** specify, clarify, plan, checklist, tasks, analyze, implement, converge. Read generated outputs and correct blocking issues between steps. The prompts below are literal messages for **Claude Desktop Code**; none is a Terminal command. *Every implement must be followed by actual tests and converge*.
##### R2-G24-01: Playable rule kernel
**Spec directory:** `specs/531-crystal-quarry-playable-rule-kernel/` • **Functional requirement:** Implement deterministic state transition and exact win/failure evaluation. **Unique game objective:** choose break lines to expose a hidden gem network in a procedural rock body. **Domain algorithm:** rock consists of bounded convex chunks from deterministic Voronoi seeds; split along known planes, not dynamic brittle FEM. **Reference solver:** seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints. **Required Stage Two dependencies:** R2-F01, R2-F02, R2-F03, R2-F04, R2-F05, R2-F06, R2-F07, R2-F11, R2-F12, R2-F16, R2-F18, R2-F22, R2-F23, R2-F24, R2-F25, R2-F26, R2-F27, R2-F28, R2-F29, R2-F30, R2-F31, R2-F32, R2-F33, R2-F34.
**Proof obligation:** demonstrate this slice works in `CrystalQuarry` and does not break any unrelated existing app. All logic path tests use the stored seed/witness; render slice tests use the existing ANGLE-backed shader host. Device-specific proof is **only planned here** until after all 25 new game targets pass simulator lock.

#### 6.24.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** fracture robustness and overly similar visuals to Faceted Forge; target differs as exploration not shaping solids. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `fracture` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `CrystalQuarry` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `CrystalQuarry` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `CrystalQuarry` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.24.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** fracture robustness and overly similar visuals to Faceted Forge; target differs as exploration not shaping solids. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `mine` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.24.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Crystal Quarry
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** choose break lines to expose a hidden gem network in a procedural rock body. **CPU domain:** terrain-contained voxel fracture network. **Ground-truth metric:** reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency. **Candidate solver:** seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints. The visual identity is black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

#### 6.24.16. Source file checklist, ownership, public boundaries, versioning
| Required file or module (proposed relative path) | Engineering responsibility | Independent acceptance and review question |
|---|---|---|
| `Apps/crystal-quarry/App/CrystalQuarryApp.swift` | Entry lifecycle, privacy, accessibility environment and native settings | Does app launch with network unavailable, no splash stall and only owned signing config? |
| `Apps/crystal-quarry/Views/GameSceneView.swift` | SwiftUI-to-VisualCore presentation bridge | Can camera/rotation changes leave canonical state hash unchanged? |
| `Apps/crystal-quarry/Views/LevelPickerView.swift` | Accessible chapters, progress and replay controls | Are locked levels due solely to local sequential progression rather than monetization? |
| `Apps/crystal-quarry/Views/SettingsView.swift` | Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, haptic/sound, control sensitivity | Does every setting work without changing puzzle success predicates? |
| `Apps/crystal-quarry/Views/TutorialView.swift` | Tactile onboarding and tutorial state graph | Can a script and an inexperienced touch user finish tutorial without guessing? |
| `Apps/crystal-quarry/Resources/Info.plist` | Minimum OS, local-only privacy descriptions and display metadata | Does packaging remain compatible with D3 iPadOS 26.5? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Domain/CrystalQuarryState.swift` | Canonical fixed-point/discrete puzzle state | Do encode/decode and repeated replay retain the same hash? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Domain/CrystalQuarryAction.swift` | Tagged commands with quantized player gestures | Are illegal inputs rejected and never silently clipped into a win? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Domain/CrystalQuarryRules.swift` | Implement reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency | Does test oracle derive from CPU model, not a visual-effect score? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Domain/CrystalQuarrySolver.swift` | Implement seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints | Does witness replay reach the terminal predicate within bounded time? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Generation/LevelFactory.swift` | Seeded candidate generation with documented salt/rejection policy | Are seeds reproducible and all authored levels reachable? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Generation/LevelValidator.swift` | Check witness, schema and per-band requirements | Can no invalid level reach the signed shipping content list? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Rendering/SceneAdapter.swift` | Convert immutable model snapshot into draw commands | Can renderer be disabled while solver still passes? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Rendering/ProceduralGeometry.swift` | Generate procedural slate shell and related meshes | Are there no required externally generated textures or meshes? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.vert` | Portable GLSL ES vertex transforms | Has native shader compilation been exercised on the configured GLES path? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Rendering/Shaders/effect.frag` | Procedural materials, tone mapping and accessibility-safe glow | Are uniforms and precision ranges guarded on D3 hardware? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Input/ActionMapper.swift` | Touch/ray-pick transform to stable command values | Can VoiceOver/stepper and gestures produce equivalent canonical actions? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Sources/Persistence/LocalSave.swift` | Versioned on-device save and transaction journal | Does a mid-write crash preserve the last complete save? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Tests/DomainTests.swift` | Pure truth predicates, illegal moves and arithmetic edges | Are boundary and failure cases asserted using deterministic oracles? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Tests/SolverTests.swift` | Witness generation and replay across all candidate seeds | Does CI refuse content without actual witness proof? |
| `Packages/Games/crystal-quarry/Tests/RenderContractTests.swift` | Shader fixtures, draw snapshot hash and fallback lanes | Does all declared material variation compile without needing imagery? |
| `Apps/crystal-quarryUITests/CrystalQuarryUITests.swift` | Simulator navigation, gestures and accessible alternative control | Does each UI journey reach a real scene and a real success/failure state? |
| `docs/games/crystal-quarry/levels/manifest.json` | Final 100 content entries, seeds, limits and expected witnessed hashes | Are all paths/binaries/source versions checksum consistent? |
| `docs/games/crystal-quarry/README.md` | Product design, mechanics, art direction and standalone identity | Would this game still be distinct if bloom were disabled? |
| `docs/test-reports/round2/crystal-quarry/device-summary.json` | Actual device evidence collected only after lock | Are D1, D2, D3 runs separate and cryptographically tied to built app? |
**File inventory rule:** all paths are proposed; reconcile with the actual VisualCore package organization and avoid duplicating existing files. Code may consolidate modules when the compiled design remains clean; document every deviation in an ADR. Never autogenerate fake `.xcresult`, signed app bundles, certificates, or device measurements.

#### 6.24.17. Architectural decision ledger — explicit choices and failure semantics
| ID | Decision to implement | Why this is required for this particular game | Verification before acceptance |

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.24.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Crystal Quarry law: `rock consists of bounded convex chunks from deterministic Voronoi seeds; split along known planes, not dynamic brittle FEM`. The source of truth is `reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

#### 6.24.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Crystal Quarry must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are select fracture seam, rotate cleavage, split chunk, expose gem, commit path. Its unique win predicate is reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


### 25. Starlight Surveyors — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G25` • **Source candidate:** `G122` • **Category:** Cosmic puzzles • **Comparative rank:** 25/25 • **Research score:** 92.84/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 82 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Rotate a 3D observatory until starlight aligns through viewports. **Signature spectacle:** geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument. **Objective:** rotate a three-axis observatory until projected star rays align through multiple lens apertures. **A failure:** a required ray passes outside a viewport on a checkpoint tick. **A victory:** all designated rays intersect their required lenses in correct sequence.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific perspective projection alignment system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.
#### 6.25.1. Player journey and minute-by-minute first play

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag gimbals, pinch zoom lens, tap lock orientation. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.25.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** perspective projection alignment. **Proposed authoritative law:** camera basis R=RzRyRx; project each star into a normalized pinhole viewport with stable near-plane constraints. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is finite camera-angle/target quantization search and analytic projective ray intersection. **Truth metric:** reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all designated rays intersect their required lenses in correct sequence” using `reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “a required ray passes outside a viewport on a checkpoint tick”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift
// `R2-G25` semantic design contract — pseudocode, adapt to current Swift toolchain.
struct StarlightSurveyorsLevel: Codable {
    let schemaVersion: Int
    let seed: UInt64
    let objectiveID: String
    let difficultyBand: Int
    let maxActions: Int
    let targetParameters: [Double]
    let obstacleDescriptors: [Double]
    let witnessInputDigest: String
}
struct StarlightSurveyorsState: Codable {
    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: rotate a three-axis observatory until projected star rays align through multiple lens apertures.
// Model: camera basis R=RzRyRx; project each star into a normalized pinhole viewport with stable near-plane constraints.
// Solver: finite camera-angle/target quantization search and analytic projective ray intersection.
```

#### 6.25.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument. **Required geometry:** procedural star sprites as points, gimbal meshes and ray tubes. **Signature shader:** Parametric star volumes, glowing triangulation rays and projection-matched constellations. **Palette:** deep ink, pearl rays and gold gears. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.25.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 82 levels. **Prototype:** angle-grid and multi-aperture puzzles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

#### 6.25.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/StarlightSurveyors/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.25.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `observatory` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “A required ray passes outside a viewport on a checkpoint tick”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
#### 6.25.12. Seed-by-seed production-level acceptance and replay contracts
Each numbered stage has *seven mandatory acceptance facets* produced by deterministic test generation. Output below enumerates the complete release catalog: QA should create all indicated artifacts and compare them to `ContentManifest.json`. The same replay witness is consumed by CPU-only unit tests and by simulator gameplay on a selected stratified subset. A stage that lacks one facet is `BLOCKED_CONTENT`, not `PASSED`.

**Game-specific measurement risk:** orientation can be disorienting; always show axes and a reset pose. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `observatory` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `StarlightSurveyors` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `StarlightSurveyors` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `StarlightSurveyors` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.25.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** orientation can be disorienting; always show axes and a reset pose. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `align` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

#### 6.25.15. Expanded production contract — Round 3–12 parity for Starlight Surveyors
**Source contract preserved:** The original 14 subsections above are unchanged. This expansion adds engineering acceptance specificity. The prior planned 80-level target is retained as a milestone (levels 001–080), while the **revised proposed ship target is 100 solver-certified levels** (081–100 are additional mastery content). No level is claimed implemented or certified until its source manifest, witness, test, and checksum exist in the actual repository. Any inability to deliver 100 valid levels is a recorded design blocker, not grounds to fabricate levels.
**Product mechanics:** rotate a three-axis observatory until projected star rays align through multiple lens apertures. **CPU domain:** perspective projection alignment. **Ground-truth metric:** reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors. **Candidate solver:** finite camera-angle/target quantization search and analytic projective ray intersection. The visual identity is geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument. Use the game-specific modes listed below; cosmetic variants do not count as new puzzle goals.
**Ten-scene product completeness checklist:** implemented 3D opening moment, direct manipulation, reversible feedback, canonical objective visualization, solvable tutorial, independent normal level, failure and retry, pause/resume and autosave, graduation/mastery presentation, and an entirely offline credits/settings surface. All screens must be reachable by deterministic UI-test hooks and by a normal user without test mode.

**Content progression acceptance:** level 001 must teach one control; levels 020/040/060/080/100 form chapter exit exercises and may not be cleared by arbitrary no-op paths. At least one alternate valid approach should be checked for every optional-mastery band, unless uniqueness is intentional and verified. All 100 must have deterministic replay; generator retry salts are logged, and content hashes are included in the final implementation lock. Challenge cannot be artificially generated by hiding targets with bloom or by requiring inaccessible touch precision.

#### 6.25.19. 80 executable acceptance-scenario designs — host/simulator first, physical devices only after lock
Each row below is a **future test requirement**. A test case is incomplete without fixture data, an executable test method, a measured/observable oracle and a stored result. Baseline Starlight Surveyors law: `camera basis R=RzRyRx; project each star into a normalized pinhole viewport with stable near-plane constraints`. The source of truth is `reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors`. Tests must never assert that an animation or screenshot alone proves the level solved.

The existing **10 features × eight literal Spec Kit skill prompts** in subsection 6.25.10 are authoritative and must all be invoked. The following expands their expected outputs and task granularity; it does not replace any `/speckit-*` invocation or eliminate `/speckit-converge`.

|---|---|---|
| `R2-G25-01` — Rule kernel | Write an explicit source specification for `rotate observatory`, encode `aperture intersection` as a typed domain condition, instrument `instrument dial glyphs` from immutable snapshots, and add failing tests for `bright rays obscure aperture`. Split the task into implementation, proof fixture, device preparation (not execution), documentation and review; record individual task IDs and bind all work to the current Git commit. Use the shared VisualCore feature dependency graph, not a copied renderer. Ensure a clean build on both target simulator runtimes and update the per-game source inventory. | Invoke exactly `/speckit-specify` → `/speckit-clarify` → `/speckit-plan` → `/speckit-checklist` → `/speckit-tasks` → `/speckit-analyze` → `/speckit-implement` → `/speckit-converge` using the full feature-specific prompts already printed in 6.25.10. #### 6.25.23. Shipping decision, commercial originality and failure-to-launch gate
**Distinct standalone promise:** Starlight Surveyors must be explainable in one sentence without the words “same as the other games, but different colors.” Primary verbs are rotate observatory, align aperture, move sightline, inspect parallax, commit alignment. Its unique win predicate is reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors. A candidate with poor D3 clarity, inadequate accessibility, an unsolved content seed, unverified premium packaging, or effectively identical gameplay to another portfolio app is not releasable even if screenshots look impressive.
**Release acceptance:** ship only after 100 real levels have witnessed solutions, all 80 QA scenarios have traced results (with justified per-runtime applicability), full accessibility journeys pass, app works in airplane/offline conditions without an account, valid icon and metadata are generated from original code assets, privacy disclosures are accurate, debug automation is absent from shipping Release, all 25 apps have completed their simulator lock, and this game has actual device evidence for D1/D2/D3. Owner-controlled signing and App Store submission remain separate permissions; do not infer approval.


## 7. Strict autonomous project schedule and task graph
**The requested chronological split is preserved:** first fully implement and simulator-verify the entire new suite; then run hardware in one D1 → D2 → D3 sequence. Stage Two cannot begin until the original README first-stage lock AND first-stage device campaign evidence are complete. Within Stage Two, simulator/host tests are part of implementation and are allowed continuously; no real-device install, launch or XCTest before Stage Two lock.
### 7.1 Overall gate ledger
| Gate | Work | Exit proof | Device access |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R2-000` | Read actual repo, original README, CLAUDE.md, the 25 source AssertionOutlines, current pins | `round1-exit-audit.json` passes with checksums and 75 first-stage device rows | read-only device inventory metadata allowed; no tests |
| `R2-001` | Implement missing shared features `R2-F01..R2-F33` in dependency order | all affected host unit and simulator/GL shader fixtures pass; each implemented feature has full Spec Kit converge | no device tests |
| `R2-002` | Implement game 01 through 25, **ten scoped features per game** | every new game solver, level catalog, rendering, native UI, accessibility, privacy and XcodeGen target implemented | no device tests |
| `R2-003` | Full suite independent simulator build matrix and genuine UI/visual inspection | all 25 new app targets build and pass required 26.5/27.2 simulator and host suites, no untracked missing tests | no device tests |
| `R2-IMPLEMENTATION-LOCK` | Freeze and verify Stage Two source revision, docs, content and binary manifest | signed machine-generated evidence manifest, all new subfeature Spec Kit convergence complete; no placeholders | still no device tests before lock pass |
| `R2-D1` | All 25 new games on iPhone 15 iOS 27.0.1 | 25 run directories, 25 device rows, actual command/exit/data hashes | D1 only |
| `R2-D2` | All 25 new games on iPad Pro M5 iPadOS 27.2 | another 25 rows with iPad-specific tests | D2 only |
| `R2-D3` | All 25 new games on iPad A16 iPadOS 26.5 | another 25 rows; sustained 30-min D3 stress per game | D3 only; **never update** |
| `R2-F34` | Suite-wide convergence, reconcile defects without erasing evidence | all affected simulator/device regressions rerun; `R2-F34` complete `/speckit-converge` | only targeted retests after entire device campaign |
| `R2-FINAL-AUDIT` | QA evidence, IP, no-ads, no-image-assets, SDK/legal, per-app completeness | audit JSON points to proofs; honest Go/Pivot/No-Go decisions for each game | no release or App Store operations by default |
